newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Deutsche Bank denies Mundial stake report.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Bank denies Mundial stake report.

text.p: Deutsche Bank de Investimento (DBI), the Portuguese unit of Germany's Deutsche Bank AG, on Monday denied a weekend newspaper report that it was seeking a stake in Portuguese insurer Mundial Confianca.

Publico newspaper reported on Saturday that DBI might buy a 20 percent stake in the insurer from Banco Comercial Portugues (BCP) as part of a restructuring of Portuguese businessman Antonio Champalimaud's financial interests.
But DBI president Rui Leao Martinho said there had been no contacts between his institution and the Champalimaud group which includes Banco Totta & Acores (BTA) and Banco Pinto & Sotto Mayor (BPSM).
"Deutsche Bank denies that there has been any contact at any level, in this specific case with BCP, with a view to taking a stake in Mundial Confianca," he told Reuters.
"You just have to look at the way the group has gone about taking stakes in other banks, which has been to buy other shareholders' stakes or to sell. The bank has a policy of all or nothing."
Quoting a source close to Champalimaud, Publico said the Portuguese group was studying how Deutsche Bank, which has already signed a cooperation agreement with Champalimaud, might buy the BCP stake.
The paper said Champalimaud was interested in stronger links with DBI since his was the only Portuguese banking group without a foreign strategic partner.

The Champalimaud group is in the process of an internal restructuring which will bring its banks under one common board of directors and streamline administration, accounting and information technology.
BCP officials were not available to comment on the report.
By 1000 GMT Mundial Confianca shares had slipped 22 escudos to 2006 and BCP was down 7 at 2,493 in generally weaker Lisbon share trading.
